headline: Robot tipping culture raises questions about AI labor economics
body: Automated systems are increasingly prompting users for gratuities, creating ambiguity around payment distribution and labor value attribution. This trend highlights a critical gap in how healthcare organizations should structure AI tool economics and vendor agreements. When clinical AI systems request tips or voluntary payments, it blurs accountability for tool performance and shifts cost burden unpredictably to end users. Healthcare systems evaluating AI vendors need explicit contractual language around total cost of ownership, including whether usage-triggered payments or voluntary contributions are permitted. Understanding these economic models becomes essential as AI adoption spreads across EHR systems, diagnostic tools, and clinical workflows where cost predictability directly impacts ROI calculations.
